chapter_note: This chapter is largely core cosmological teaching (three stabilizing "rocks" set within the worlds), with a brief hagiographic opening (¶1) and a late institutional/application graft in ¶5 that relocates the third rock into "the holy church" (consistent with the strong editorial fatigue signal in the second half).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue-frame opening (“Once again…to his disciples”), characteristic of the later Kephalaia editorial apparatus.

paragraphs.core_text: Three great rocks, which exist, were appointed by the greatness. They were set in these outer worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal, structural exposition establishing a numbered cosmological triad placed within “these outer worlds,” with no audience address or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the first rock is the [Pillar] of Glory, the Perfect Man, which was summoned [by the] glorious Ambassador. He set it in this zone; [ ... he] brought forth its base (?) from the earth to heaven. It bore up under the [en]tire uni[verse], and became first of all the weight-carriers in [it]s powers. In its firmness it has been set upright, and has made fast every [t]hing above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological architecture: named beings (Perfect Man, Ambassador), spatial placement (“this zone”), and a function-description of stability/weight-bearing within the universe—classic substrate voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second great and glorious rock is the new earth of light, which was set upon the earth of darkness. It has squashed the fastenings of the five storehouses of death. It has established firmness, with great firmness, over and beyond the earth of darkness. It has flattened, crushed and fixed the root of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos→cosmos mapping of a stabilizing structure (“new earth of light”) acting upon underworld architecture (“storehouses of death”), with mechanistic verbs and no institutional referents.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] third rock is the great thought, which was summoned from Jesus, the glorious one.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional/application continuation: “He set it in the holy church. The church gathered in upon it, and has lived in [it]. It has stood firm, with a true fixity, for ever.” This shifts from a cosmological origin statement to identifying the rock with the contemporary/institutional church (cosmos→church pointing).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens in cosmological register (a named cosmic source, “Jesus, the glorious one,” functioning as a being in the system), then pivots to an ecclesial anchoring (“holy church”), indicating later editorial application consistent with chapter’s second-half pastoral drift.

paragraphs.core_text: [These] are the three great rocks, they that have come forth in great confidence, in three great and honoured places. They were appointed and distributed in three great places of these [self]same worlds. They were made fast according to the will of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure in the same impersonal, cosmological voice: reiterates triadic placement “in…worlds” and divine appointment without doxology, citation, or institutional extension.
